subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Organ-specific toxicities of cytotoxics: mechanisms, clinical manifestations and specific antidotes

steps.tx: Cardiotoxicity from anthracycline chemotherapy stems from specific nuclear enzymatic interactions and oxidative injury. Direct binding of doxorubicin to **topoisomerase II-beta** inside adult cardiomyocytes triggers persistent double-strand DNA breaks, defective mitochondrial biogenesis, and excessive **free radical** generation. The resulting iron-dependent reactive oxygen species induce irreversible myocyte apoptosis, myofibrillar loss, and late progressive dilated cardiomyopathy refractory to inotropic support.
steps.say: Cardiotoxicity from anthracycline chemotherapy stems from specific nuclear enzymatic interactions and oxidative injury. Direct binding of doxorubicin to topoisomerase II-beta inside adult cardiomyocytes triggers persistent DNA breaks, defective mitochondrial biogenesis, and excessive free radical generation. The resulting reactive oxygen species induce irreversible myocyte apoptosis and late dilated cardiomyopathy.

steps.tx: Pulmonary parenchymal injury from antineoplastic glycopeptides is mediated by deficient hydrolytic clearance. **Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity** manifests initially as subacute cough and dyspnoea, progressing to organizing alveolitis and fatal **pulmonary fibrosis**. The lung lacks bleomycin hydrolase, leaving pulmonary tissue vulnerable to iron-oxygen radical injury. High concentrations of supplemental inspired oxygen during anaesthesia accelerate alveolar damage; perioperative fraction of inspired oxygen FiO2 must be strictly minimized.

left.title: Bleomycin Toxicity Risk Factors
points: Age > 40 to 60 years and prior chest radiation

right.title: Clinical Surveillance & Management
points: Serial DLCO monitoring (stop if DLCO falls > 20-25%)
High-resolution chest CT: bibasilar subpleural fibrosis
High-dose systemic corticosteroids in early alveolitis

steps.tx: Platinum accumulation in the proximal renal tubules provokes heavy metal nephrotoxicity. **Cisplatin nephrotoxicity** causes acute tubular necrosis, marked renal vasoconstriction, and prominent **magnesium wasting** through damaged ascending loop and distal tubule transport channels. Vigorous intravenous pre- and post-hydration with 1 to 2 litres of normal saline containing potassium chloride and magnesium sulphate accelerates urinary flow and mitigates acute kidney injury.
steps.say: Platinum accumulation in the proximal renal tubules provokes heavy metal nephrotoxicity. Cisplatin nephrotoxicity causes acute tubular necrosis, marked renal vasoconstriction, and prominent magnesium wasting through damaged tubular transport channels. Vigorous intravenous pre- and post-hydration with normal saline containing electrolytes accelerates urinary flow and mitigates nephrotoxic risk.

nodes.label: Mitigated by Pre/Post Normal Saline Hydration

steps.tx: Oxazaphosphorine bioactivation produces neurotoxic aldehyde metabolites that cross the blood-brain barrier. **Ifosfamide neurotoxicity** presents as progressive lethargy, confusion, cerebellar ataxia, cranial nerve palsies, and hallucinations, mediated by hepatic production of chloroacetaldehyde. Intravenous **methylene blue** at 50 mg every 4 hours acts as an effective therapeutic and prophylactic agent by serving as an electron acceptor, restoring depleted mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes.

rows: Acute renal failure with MTX retention

steps.tx: Severe nephrotoxicity during high-dose methotrexate therapy arrests physiological drug elimination. **Glucarpidase** recombinant carboxypeptidase G2 provides rapid, life-saving enzymatic rescue during **methotrexate** induced acute kidney injury. Administered intravenously, glucarpidase rapidly cleaves circulating extracellular methotrexate into inactive glutamate and DAMPA within 15 minutes, lowering circulating toxic methotrexate concentrations by over 95%, permitting renal functional recovery without systemic tissue accumulation.

nodes.label: Cleaves MTX into Inactive DAMPA + Glutamate

steps.tx: Platin-induced peripheral sensory nerve injury features two distinct chronological and mechanistic phases. **Oxaliplatin-induced** neurotoxicity begins as an acute, cold-triggered transient neuropathy characterized by peripheral **dysaesthesia**, perioral tingling, and pharyngolaryngeal dysaesthesia provoked by voltage-gated sodium channel dysfunction. In contrast, cumulative exposure exceeding 780 to 850 mg/m2 causes structural sensory axonopathy, sensory ataxia, and permanent functional impairment, managed with planned chemotherapy holidays.
steps.say: Platin-induced peripheral sensory nerve injury features two distinct chronological and mechanistic phases. Oxaliplatin-induced neurotoxicity begins as an acute, cold-triggered transient neuropathy characterized by peripheral dysaesthesia and pharyngolaryngeal spasm provoked by sodium channel dysfunction. In contrast, cumulative exposure exceeding 780 mg/m2 causes permanent sensory axonopathy.

left.title: Acute Cold-Induced Neuropathy
points: Onset within hours of oxaliplatin infusion
Triggered by cold beverages or touching cold objects
Reversible dysfunction of neuronal sodium channels

right.title: Chronic Cumulative Sensory Axonopathy
points: Impaired proprioception, vibratory sense, and ataxia
Slow, incomplete recovery over months to years

steps.tx: Topoisomerase I inhibitors inflict delayed gastrointestinal toxicity through biliary excretion of active metabolites. Irinotecan-induced delayed **secretory diarrhoea** emerging more than 24 hours post-infusion is caused by active SN-38 damaging intestinal epithelial crypt cells. Management requires immediate high-dose **loperamide** at 4 mg at onset followed by 2 mg every 2 hours until the patient is diarrhoea-free for 12 consecutive hours, adding oral fluoroquinolones if diarrhoea persists beyond 24 hours.
steps.say: Topoisomerase I inhibitors inflict delayed gastrointestinal toxicity through biliary excretion of active metabolites. Irinotecan-induced delayed secretory diarrhoea emerging more than 24 hours post-infusion is caused by active SN-38 damaging intestinal crypt cells. Management requires immediate high-dose loperamide at 4 mg initially followed by 2 mg every 2 hours until diarrhoea resolves.

steps.tx: Continuous infusion of fluoropyrimidines carries an unpredictable risk of severe cardiotoxicity. 5-Fluorouracil cardiotoxicity manifests as typical angina, dynamic ischemic ST changes, **coronary vasospasm**, ventricular arrhythmias, or fulminant **cardiogenic shock**. Vasospasm is unrelated to underlying coronary artery stenosis and requires immediate termination of the fluoropyrimidine infusion, continuous electrocardiographic monitoring, sublingual or intravenous nitroglycerin, and oral dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, avoiding drug re-exposure.
steps.say: Continuous infusion of fluoropyrimidines carries an unpredictable risk of severe cardiotoxicity. 5-Fluorouracil cardiotoxicity manifests as typical angina, dynamic ischemic ST changes, coronary vasospasm, ventricular arrhythmias, or fulminant cardiogenic shock. Vasospasm requires immediate termination of the infusion, continuous ECG monitoring, nitrates, and calcium channel blockers, avoiding drug re-exposure.

rows: Stop infusion, IV nitrates, calcium blockers
Loss of HER2 cardioprotective survival signals
Asymptomatic left ventricular ejection fraction drop
Hold drug, ACE inhibitors; usually reversible
